summary: Manually Remove Stuck Parts and Delete Work Order S-100
reported_issue: Parts on Work Order S-100 (customer Antares Hire NZ Ltd) are stuck and cannot be removed; request to the backend team to manually remove the stuck parts and delete WO S-100.
expected_after_fix: The work order (and its stuck parts) can be removed; a WO with awaiting/stuck parts should be deletable rather than blocked.
steps_i_followed: Noted S-100 / Antares Hire NZ is a specific production record (this staging org is Foothills Group Inc); tested the general regression it implies instead
Used disposable WO S9-24938 (3c12bbfa) which had 3 awaiting part_requests across 2 lines
Opened the WO-level kebab (Audit Log / Timesheets / Delete Work Order) and chose Delete Work Order
Observed the confirmation dialog and confirmed deletion, capturing the API response
actual_now: The WO with awaiting parts deleted successfully. The confirm dialog explicitly stated 'There are awaiting parts. Are you sure you want to delete this work order?' with Delete/Cancel; clicking Delete fired POST /api/work-orders/delete which returned HTTP 201 with {work_order_id: 3c12bbfa...} and redirected to the work-orders list. Awaiting/stuck parts do NOT block deletion; the system warns and allows it.
notes: The specific S-100 / Antares Hire NZ incident is a prod-only manual data fix not reproducible on staging. The general regression (a work order with stuck/awaiting parts cannot be deleted) does NOT reproduce: a WO with awaiting parts is deletable via the UI (201). This also cleaned up the disposable test WO. Confidence medium because only the general delete behavior, not the exact S-100 record, could be exercised.
